title: Employees Hired After 2022
description:
Return the name and hire date of every employee who was hired **after December 31, 2022** (i.e. hire date is in 2023 or later).

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| hire_date | DATE |

Output columns: `name`, `hire_date`. Order by `hire_date` ascending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, hire_date DATE); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', DATE '2021-03-15'), (2, 'Bob', DATE '2022-11-01'), (3, 'Carol', DATE '2023-01-10'), (4, 'Dan', DATE '2023-07-22'), (5, 'Eve', DATE '2024-02-28');
solution_sql: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE hire_date > DATE '2022-12-31' ORDER BY hire_date
hints: Use a WHERE clause with a date comparison.
DATE '2022-12-31' is the last day of 2022; use > to exclude it.
explanation: Comparing `hire_date > DATE '2022-12-31'` filters to employees hired from 2023 onward. Carol (Jan 2023), Dan (Jul 2023), and Eve (Feb 2024) qualify; Alice and Bob do not.
